theme: Divine manifestation is not ordinary birth; it arises through the Lord’s own nature and purpose.
context: Krishna says that although he is unborn, imperishable, and the Lord of beings, he comes into being by his own Maya while presiding over his own nature. The next verse, 4.7, speaks of his manifestation when dharma declines.
contextHindi: कृष्ण कहते हैं कि वे अजन्मा, अविनाशी और सभी प्राणियों के ईश्वर हैं। फिर भी अपनी प्रकृति पर अधिकार रखते हुए वे अपनी माया से प्रकट होते हैं। धर्म में गिरावट के समय प्रकट होने की बात अगले श्लोक, 4.7 में आती है।
sanskritDevanagari:
अजोऽपि सन्नव्ययात्मा भूतानामीश्वरोऽपि सन् |
प्रकृतिं स्वामधिष्ठाय सम्भवाम्यात्ममायया ||४-६||
transliteration:
ajo.api sannavyayātmā bhūtānāmīśvaro.api san .
prakṛtiṃ svāmadhiṣṭhāya sambhavāmyātmamāyayā ||4-6||

wordByWord.meaning: unborn; not coming forth from ordinary causation
of beings; of all living entities
Lord; the supreme controller and guide

spokenHindi: कृष्ण इस श्लोक में कहते हैं कि वे अजन्मा हैं, उनका स्वरूप अविनाशी है, और वे सभी प्राणियों के ईश्वर हैं। फिर भी वे अपनी प्रकृति पर अधिकार रखते हुए अपनी माया से प्रकट होते हैं। “अजोऽपि सन्नव्ययात्मा” का अर्थ है: अजन्मा होते हुए भी, अविनाशी स्वरूप वाले। “प्रकृतिं स्वामधिष्ठाय” का भाव है कि वे अपनी प्रकृति के अधिष्ठाता हैं। यहाँ “माया” का अर्थ कृष्ण की अपनी शक्ति है। श्लोक 4.5 में कृष्ण अपने और अर्जुन के अनेक बीते जन्मों की बात करते हैं; यहाँ वे अपने अजन्मा और अविनाशी स्वरूप के साथ प्रकट होने की बात जोड़ते हैं। इस श्लोक में यह नहीं बताया गया कि वे किस कारण से प्रकट होते हैं। धर्म में गिरावट और अधर्म के बढ़ने पर प्रकट होने की बात अगले श्लोक 4.7 में आती है। इसलिए इन दोनों श्लोकों को पढ़ते हुए 4.6 के कथन और 4.7 के कथन में अंतर रखना उपयोगी है।
clearEnglish: Krishna says that he is unborn, imperishable in nature, and the Lord of all beings. Yet, presiding over his own nature, he comes into being by his own Maya. The supplied translation gives the verse’s claim; it does not say here why Krishna manifests. The word Maya is retained from the verse and translation rather than used to add a separate explanation. Verse 4.5 speaks of Krishna and Arjuna having had many births, with Krishna knowing them all. Verse 4.6 adds that Krishna is unborn and imperishable, yet appears through his own nature and Maya. The reason for manifestation when dharma declines is given in the next verse, 4.7, not in this one. Keeping that distinction clear lets us hear what 4.6 actually says without assigning it a teaching from the verses that follow.

interpretationPerspectives.label: TEXT
interpretationPerspectives.explanation: The verse states that Krishna is unborn, imperishable, and the Lord of beings, yet he appears by his own power through his own nature. This is a direct statement of divine sovereignty and timelessness.

interpretationPerspectives.label: VERSE DISTINCTION
interpretationPerspectives.explanation: The supplied edition gives no separate commentary under 4.6. The protection of the good, destruction of the wicked, and establishment of dharma are stated in verse 4.8; the decline of dharma is mentioned in 4.7.

interpretationPerspectives.label: INFERENCE
interpretationPerspectives.explanation: A careful conclusion is that the verse presents Krishna’s manifestation as occurring through his own nature and Maya, although he is unborn and imperishable. It does not give the reason for that manifestation; the next verses address that.

practicalApplication.label: See the larger order
practicalApplication.text: When life feels uncertain, pause to distinguish what you know from what you are assuming. This verse describes Krishna’s own nature and manifestation; it does not ask you to explain every difficult event.

practicalApplication.label: Stay with the verse
practicalApplication.text: Read the verse slowly and notice its specific claims: Krishna is unborn and imperishable, is the Lord of beings, and appears through his own nature and Maya. Keep these statements distinct from the reason for manifestation given in the following verses.

reflectionQuestion: What does this verse say about Krishna’s nature and how he appears?
reflectionQuestionHindi: यह श्लोक कृष्ण के स्वरूप और उनके प्रकट होने के बारे में क्या कहता है?
